title: Why Titanic Skimped on Lifeboats
topic: Why the Titanic carried too few lifeboats

lines: A shipyard foreman hoists a massive wooden lifeboat onto a crane, sweat dripping.
The crew laughs, saying “We have enough – the law only asks for this many.”
Titanic rolls out of Belfast with twenty boats, but only sixteen can be launched from the davits.
Two emergency cutters sit hanging, ready, while four collapsibles are stored upside‑down on the officers’ roof.
You see, it’s like packing a school bus with only a few seat belts – you feel unsafe even before an accident.
The Board of Trade required ships over ten‑thousand tons to carry just sixteen lifeboats for 990 people.
White Star chose to exceed that rule, fitting twenty boats that could hold 1,178 souls – still only a third of the 2,200 aboard.
Because the law was so lax, the “extra” boats were never fully integrated, leaving half the ship without a quick escape route.

claims.claim: Titanic carried twenty lifeboats: fourteen standard, two cutters, four collapsibles, four more than Board of Trade regulations.
The lifeboats could accommodate 1,178 people – about one‑third of those on board.
Board of Trade regulations at the time required only sixteen lifeboats for ships over 10,000 tons, enough for 990 occupants.
Two emergency cutters were kept swung out for immediate use, while four collapsible boats were stored upside‑down and hard to launch.
